messages:
tara: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing "staged hash-chaining" for air-gapped upgrades. Idea: produce a sequence of signed artifacts where each delta manifest includes the hash of the previous applied state, plus an optional migration step. This gives a verifiable upgrade path without reaching back to a central repo.

mike: short version: chain each delta to previous via hash, sign the chain, runtime verifies chain and applies one step at a time, canary by flipping a local flag?

tara: yup. sketch of invariants: 1) every delta is signed by a team key (KMS/HSM). 2) each delta manifest contains previous_root_hash and post_apply_hash. 3) verifier applies deltas in order and verifies post_apply_hash after each step. 4) runtime keeps a compact state anchor on disk (current_root_hash) for crash recovery.

jin: what about rollback? storing reverse deltas will bloat bundles. could we instead keep periodic full snapshots + small deltas?

tara: agree. tradeoff: snapshot frequency vs delta chain length. snapshot = faster rollback + simpler recovery; delta-only = smaller airgap payloads. propose snapshot every N major releases (configurable).

anika: also think about interface boundaries: packager -> signer -> publisher are separate. packager emits unsigned bundle, signer attaches signatures and metadata (issuer, cert id, signing key id), publisher stamps transport metadata. runtime only consumes signed manifests and verifier lib. this keeps verifier minimal.

mike: good. suggests we formalize the manifest envelope to avoid ad-hoc fields. maybe use COSE or a tiny envelope: {"meta":..., "prev":..., "payload_hash":..., "sig":...}. keep it stable.

jin: runtime resource concerns: verifying long chains (100+ deltas) might be expensive on <8GB hosts. mitigation: verifier should short-circuit to the nearest snapshot anchor when available. also allow offline pre-verify during staging (packager can produce a verified sequence file).

tara: exact example manifest snippet (informal):
```json
{
  "version": "1.2",
  "issuer": "redwood-release-team",
  "prev_root_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "payload": "delta-v2-to-v3.tar.gz",
  "payload_hash": "sha256:ffff...",
  "post_apply_hash": "sha256:eeee...",
  "signatures": [{"key_id":"sig-2026-03","sig":"BASE64..."}]
}
```

anika: question re: KMS/HSM: packager and signer run in CI with access to signing key. for private deployments we need a rotation story and local customer HSM support. signer should emit metadata about key provenance so runtime can decide trust (e.g., customer-root vs redwood-root).

mike: add to that: verifier must accept a trust policy file (local). default uses redwood root cert pinned. customers can supply additional anchors. verifier API: verify(chain_manifest, trust_anchors, apply_dir, rollback_dir) -> status. keep it tiny.

jin: atomic apply: we need on-disk staging. plan: write to staging partition, verify post_apply_hash, then swap symlink/rename to live. if swap fails, bootloader must still point to previous live. need power-failure tests.

tara: agreed. also add fast rollback switch: local flag file that runtime monitors; ops can flip it via console or out-of-band. flips trigger verifier to re-apply nearest snapshot or reverse snapshot if available.

anika: ops UX: when we publish bundles to customers, include a small index file that lists the chain heads + snapshot anchors. this lets on-prem updater fetch only necessary files from media. important for constrained USB images.

mike: CI/automation note: packager pipeline should produce an artifact index with sizes and chunk checksums so customers can prefetch on slow networks. also generate an "apply plan" for each target host type (arm64 vs x86).

jin: migration tooling: some upgrades change on-disk schema. we should version migration steps and make them idempotent. add a dry-run mode that returns the expected post_apply_hash without touching disk.

tara: TODOs from this thread: 1) I will draft a concise RFC section on manifest envelope + verifier API. 2) mike, can you prototype staging swap logic in runtime? 3) jin, please enumerate memory/CPU constraints and propose short-circuit heuristics for chains >M deltas. 4) anika, write key provenance and trust-anchor UX for private deployments.

anika: ack. adding rotation notes and HSM examples to doc.

infra-bot: CI: link to draft RFC: https://go.redwood/repo/rfc/staged-hash-chaining (checks: spell, linter) :white_check_mark:

mike: one last thought — telemetry: runtime should log applied_root_hash, applied_manifest_id, and verification_result to console (non-sensitive). keep minimal so customers can decide what to ship to us.

tara: perfect. I'll post the draft RFC later today and tag y'all for comments. thanks all :rocket:
